title: The $33.86 Billion Financial Disaster That Shocked America! #Shorts
description:
In the late 1980s, America's savings and loan industry faced a massive financial crisis. Hundreds of institutions failed, and taxpayers faced billions of dollars in costs.

On September 9, 1988, Financial Corporation of America, the parent of American Savings and Loan, filed for bankruptcy with $33.86 billion in assets. From 1986 to 1995, 1,043 thrifts failed, and the cost to taxpayers was about $124 billion.

Sources: FRED (Federal Funds Rate), FDIC Banking Review 2000 (Curry & Shibut, "The Cost of the Savings and Loan Crisis"), Federal Reserve History ("Savings and Loan Crisis").

This video is for educational purposes only and is not financial advice.
